_comment: Static permissions.deny rules merged into ~/.claude/settings.json by bin/mc-guard.sh.
These are the cheap first line; guards/guard-bash.sh does the robust parse.
Both layers are needed: the Claude Code permissions docs warn that Bash patterns
constraining arguments are fragile, and a rule cannot consult git status.
deny is evaluated before ask and allow, and the first match wins, so these hold
even though the allow list contains a bare "Bash". A deny rule also matches past
leading env assignments, so Bash(sudo *) still catches FOO=bar sudo id.
Only unconditionally-wrong commands live here. Anything context-dependent (git
checkout on a clean tree is fine, on a dirty tree it is not) belongs in the hook.
The sed/perl entries deliberately match only the leading '-i' form. The broader
'sed *-i*' also matches any filename containing '-i' (sed -e 's/x/y/' build-init.sh),
which would deny legitimate commands. guard-bash.sh parses the argument list properly
and catches the clustered and wrapped forms, so nothing is lost by narrowing here.
